# David Buchanan

Nationwide, London, South West, International

[david@subtext-translations.com](mailto:david@subtext-translations.com)

I have been audio describing since 2010. Over the years I've tackled everything from soap operas to David Lynch, and still love the challenge that each project brings, balancing expressiveness and emotion with clarity and concision. 

Having studied film at undergrad and postgrad levels, then written and directed several films of my own, I have a strong grasp of cinematic storytelling techniques. This helps me to understand the filmmaker’s visual decisions, to communicate them clearly, and to prioritise what matters most when space is tight.

# Jake Hayes

East Midlands, West Midlands, London, South West, Wales

[popriot@gmail.com](mailto:popriot@gmail.com)

I'm an audio describer based in the south west. I trained with Roz Chalmers from The National Theatre audio description team in 2021 on a programme supported by Arts Council England for Theatre Royal, Bath. 

I've been working in theatres across the south west ever since, regularly describing shows and running touch tours at the Bristol Old Vic since 2022. I've also worked on for the Tobacco Factory in Bristol and The Mayflower Southampton, describing classic and contemporary theatre, musicals, ballet and family shows. I'm happy to work alone or with another describer and am interested in expanding my practice into other areas, such as audio guides, museums, visual arts and gardens. 

As a former TV producer for BBC Arts, I'm also technically proficient and have provided pre-recorded AD for the Bristol Old Vic. Earlier in my career I worked for three years at BBC radio Bristol where I acted as assistant producer and guide to a blind producer. This led to working with the RNIB as a guide for deafblind people in the Bristol area.

# Sarah Borges

Nationwide, East of England, London, International

[sarahborges@mac.com](mailto:sarahborges@mac.com)

An American-born, British-trained actor, Sarah expanded her voice acting career into the field of Audio Description in 2015 after working on audiobook recordings for the RNIB in London. She quickly progressed to scripting projects as well as voicing them, working across a wide range of content, including animations, documentaries, feature films, and television series. In recent years, she has broadened her expertise to include voicing subtitles alongside AD and providing live AD scripting and voicing. Her projects have included live AD work for circus performances at the Out There Festival in Great Yarmouth and Bernstein's Trouble in Tahiti and A Quiet Place at the Royal Opera House.

Sarah collaborates with production companies around the world, contributing to projects for clients such as Netflix, NBC Universal, Turner, Disney, TCM, Apple, and Amazon. Having lived equally on both sides of the Atlantic, Sarah brings a unique versatility to her work, delivering accent and dialect precision tailored to both US and UK audiences with the highest professional standards.
